raw_case_text: Case 6: A 29 year old patient that reported exanthema and pruritus in the second trimester of gestation. Her IgM serology was positive for Zika and the PRNT90% was positive for neutralizing antibodies. At 38 weeks of gestation, her baby girl was born by cesarean that presented a cephalic circumference of 30 cm.

subjective.chief_complaint: 29-year-old pregnant female in the second trimester of gestation presenting with exanthema and pruritus.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced acute onset of a pruritic exanthema during the second trimester of pregnancy. The pregnancy progressed until 38 weeks of gestation, when she delivered a baby girl by cesarean section who presented with microcephaly.
subjective.past_medical_history: Second trimester of pregnancy; no prior medical illnesses reported.

objective.physical_examination: Maternal: Cutaneous exanthema. Neonatal: Female infant delivered at 38 weeks gestation by cesarean section with a cephalic circumference of 30 cm (microcephaly).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Congenital Zika syndrome manifest as neonatal microcephaly following maternal second-trimester Zika virus infection. Maternal infection was confirmed by positive Zika IgM serology and positive PRNT90% for neutralizing antibodies. Delivery occurred at 38 weeks gestation with the neonate demonstrating microcephaly (head circumference 30 cm).
